name: Keel-Timber of the Argo's Sister
description: A beam of oak from a hull that was built from the same grove as the famous one.
benefit: Lets a settlement rebuild a ship or bridge in half the time and cost.
cost: Fourteen kilograms of awkward length that cannot be carried with a drawn weapon.

name: Raw Orichalcum Lode
description: A lump of unworked ore the size of a head, still sweating in the cold.
benefit: Refines into a large store of charge at a forge.
cost: It is heavy enough to cripple the carrier and irresistible to thieves.

name: Reliquary of Pyre Ash
description: A sealed bronze box of ash from a pyre that should have been lit a generation ago.
benefit: Lays a restless grave to rest with a single scattering.
cost: One use only, and it commits the bearer to attend that funeral, in person, on the day.

name: Heart of a Wild Thing
description: Preserved in honey and wrapped in leaves of a tree that no longer grows here.
benefit: A rare input for the finest craft: leather, bowstring or drum.
cost: Worth more to hunters and fences than to any craftsman. Carrying it draws both.

name: Stack of Oracle Bones
description: Knuckle bones scratched with questions that were never answered.
benefit: Trades to any priesthood as proof of access to the dead correspondence.
cost: A priesthood that buys them owns the questions too, and the bearer is asked to answer them.

name: The Hegemon's Seal Matrix
description: The die from which imperial seals were struck, found in a cellar that was meant to be flooded.
benefit: Can forge a seal of passage, once, in any place the Hegemony ever ruled.
cost: Forgery is a capital offence in every city it was ever valid in.

name: Silt of the Styx
description: Black silt from a river bank no living person has stood on.
benefit: Seals an oath into a document, a body or a door so it cannot be broken.
cost: The seal binds the one who applied it too. Whatever they sealed, they are held to.

name: Spool of Labyrinth Thread
description: Red thread that is longer than the spool it is wound on.
benefit: Marks a path that cannot be lost, in any dungeon or maze, for one entry.
cost: It leads out. It does not tell the bearer what they will have to pass on the way.
